sections.h2: Which city office handles your tax bill
sections.html:
Farmington Hills divides the work in two: the Treasury Division mails and collects the real and personal property tax, and the Assessing Division sets a value on every parcel. Both offices share a building at 31555 West Eleven Mile Road, Farmington Hills, MI 48336, and serve the public on weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30. The Treasury number is 248-871-2480 and Assessing answers at 248-871-2470.

The city lies in Oakland County. Whatever the city has not collected by early March moves to the county treasurer, and the city can no longer accept payment. The address for your check changes along with the cost of lateness.

Farmington Hills uses two bills a year. The summer bill is due without penalty from July 1 to August 31, and the winter bill from December 1 to February 16. The city's property tax page sets out the full calendar.

Farmington Hills summer and winter bill calendar
MilestoneSummer billWinter bill
MailedJune 30November 30

A bill that never arrived still carries the tax and any late charges. After a purchase, a move or a land contract, tell Assessing so the next bill reaches the right person.

sections.h2: How an assessment is set and challenged
sections.html:
The city aims for an assessed value equal to half of market value. Assessing studies 24 months of sales so that similar homes land in line, and each parcel is tied to a parcel number, a legal description and an address.

The State Tax Commission recommends reviewing roughly a fifth of properties each year, so an appraiser may stop by to look at your exterior. Notices of assessment go out every February, laying out the proposed valuation, the property class, principal residence exemption status, transfer status and appeal rights.

  • Read the February notice and the record card for errors in square footage, class or exemption status.
  • Call 248-871-2470 for an informal meeting with the assessor or staff before the March Board of Review.
  • Take a written appeal or an appointment request to the Board of Review in March.
  • Ask for copies of your records by phone or in person. Broader requests go through the City Clerk as a records request.

If you think your value is too high, collect recent sales of similar homes nearby and bring them to the meeting. Bill due dates run on their own calendar, so an open appeal doesn't pause payment.

sections.h2: How to pay a Farmington Hills bill
sections.html:
The city recommends echecks, which post the same day with no fee. If one bounces, a $30 insufficient-funds charge follows.

  • Debit or credit card online, or by phone at 734-402-8271, for 2.8% plus 50 cents per payment.
  • In person at the Treasury counter during office hours.
  • A drive-up drop box in front of Police Headquarters, for checks only.
  • Mail to the city lockbox in Detroit, where payment counts when it is received, not when it is postmarked.

Confirm the parcel ID first, since sending money to the wrong property is the taxpayer's problem. A mailed payment needs the bill's top coupon and a check with your parcel number and phone number written on it. Don't mail after the due date.

Balances still open on March 2 pass to the Oakland County Treasurer. Older years are already with the county, and checks go to the Oakland County Treasurer at 1200 N Telegraph Road, Pontiac, Michigan 48341-0479. Call the county at 248-858-0611.

Before picking a closing date, get a payoff number from the county. MCL 211.135 calls for certificates from the county and city treasurers on tax liens and five years of payments before certain deeds can be recorded, which is why a title company wants any balance cleared at the table.

The city publishes a deferment application for summer taxes on a principal residence. The 2026 form set a household income limit of $40,000. A qualifying owner could defer the summer bill until February 16, 2027. Qualifying owners are at least 62, or totally and permanently disabled, blind, hemiplegic, paraplegic or quadriplegic, or an eligible serviceperson, veteran, widow or widower.

Assessing can answer questions about the homestead exemption, hardship or veteran's exemptions and taxable value. The city also links a list of state property tax assistance programs. Ask Treasury for the current year's form before summer bills go out, since the form is filed each year and the income limit can change.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Farmington Hills
sections.html:
Farmington Hills covers 33.31 square miles in Oakland County, bordered by West Bloomfield to the north, Franklin and Southfield to the east, Livonia to the south and Novi to the west. Almost all of the city is in Farmington Public Schools, and small portions are in Clarenceville and Walled Lake Consolidated. The main roads are M-5, Orchard Lake Road, 12 Mile Road, I-696 and I-275, with SMART buses serving the area.

An estimated 83,291 residents lived here as of July 2025, 0.9% fewer than the 2020 base. A typical owned home is valued at $354,500, and owners occupy 64.7% of housing. Households number 35,529 with a median income of $104,836, and renters pay a median of $1,551 a month. These are citywide medians, and individual blocks will differ.

sections.h2: What a seller owes at closing besides property tax
sections.html:
The state transfer tax, $3.75 per $500 of value under MCL 207.525, lands on the grantor under MCL 207.523. It is paid to the county treasurer inside 15 days of the deed being delivered.

A county transfer tax and recording fees come on top, and Oakland County's register sets its own charges. Before signing, ask the closing agent for a written statement showing the tax certificate, any open summer or winter balance and the recording costs.

A few steps help the closing go smoothly:

  1. Confirm that the summer bill and the winter bill are both paid or that the open balance is on the statement.
  2. If a balance has moved to Oakland County, call 248-858-0611 for a payoff.
  3. Tell Assessing about the sale so the next bill goes to the buyer.
  4. Keep your parcel ID handy, since every payment and certificate is tied to it.

A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender, but the same tax certificate and payoff work still applies.

faqs.q: When is the winter tax bill due in Farmington Hills?
faqs.a: December 1 through February 16 without penalty. The bill is mailed November 30, and a 4% penalty is added on February 17.

faqs.q: Where do I pay old Farmington Hills taxes?
faqs.a: At the Oakland County Treasurer, not the city. Taxes from earlier years have been turned over to the county at 1200 N Telegraph Road in Pontiac, phone 248-858-0611.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay Farmington Hills property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes. Card payments add 2.8% plus $0.50. Echecks have no fee, though a returned one costs $30.

faqs.q: How do I contest my Farmington Hills assessment?
faqs.a: Call Assessing at 248-871-2470 for an informal meeting, then use the March Board of Review, either by appointment or by letter received before the last meeting day.

faqs.q: Can seniors delay Farmington Hills summer taxes?
faqs.a: Possibly. The city's deferment form covers owners 62 or older, or disabled, blind or a qualifying veteran or surviving spouse, under a household income limit that was $40,000 on the 2026 form. Ask Treasury for the current form.
